text: 🤝🌊 "Mexico will be, without a doubt, the world leader in sargassum management." "This is the most complete response sargassum has ever received anywhere in the world. No more isolated efforts — today there is one single effort, and it belongs to all of Mexico." — Iván Chávez, Grupo Vidanta After years of every hotel and municipality fighting alone, hoteliers now sit at one table with the Navy, federal and state governments and scientists — sharing techniques, barriers and data.

🏆🌊 2025 and 2026 are the two biggest sargassum-collection years in Quintana Roo's history. "Attention to sargassum is no longer just an immediate response — it is a permanent State policy." — Mexican Navy, strategy briefing 96,151 tons collected so far in 2026 — already more than all of 2025 (92,782 tons). A 2,635.6M-peso expansion adds 2 oceanic vessels, 6 semi-oceanic ones, 35 km of barriers, early-warning monitoring and a dock in Puerto Juárez.

🛡️🌊 The Navy's mission: catch the sargassum before it touches the beach. "We have to invert this graph: collect mainly at sea, so it doesn't reach the beaches, and give the sargassum a final destination in industry." — Adm. Raymundo Morales, Navy Secretary A first 768.7M-peso stage lifts at-sea collection capacity to 1,870 tons/day: 2 tugboats, 6 coastal sargassum vessels, more dynamic barriers and ~50 km of containment barriers in the five most critical zones.

📈🌊 Sargassum in 2026: 27 times the historical average. "In 2026 it was 4 times more than in 2025. And we have 27 times more than the historical average. This has been a really difficult, atypical year." — Alicia Bárcena, Environment Secretary Up to 90,538 tons of sargassum per day are drifting in the Mexican Caribbean; about 10% reaches Quintana Roo's coasts. Mexico will host an EU-backed international sargassum summit in Cancún on October 1-2, with Japan offering support with collection vessels.

🌊💰 Mexico puts 2 billion pesos behind the fight against sargassum. "The Government of Mexico is putting up 2 billion pesos for the comprehensive handling of sargassum. The best barriers in Quintana Roo and in the entire world will be installed to protect the beaches." — President Claudia Sheinbaum The plan: intercept the algae at sea with more sargassum-collecting vessels, ~50 km of containment barriers across Cancún, Playa del Carmen, Puerto Morelos, Tulum and Mahahual, and standardized beach cleanup that doesn't strip away sand.

AGWEB: Beyond Trade: Lighthizer Says Immigration, Cartels Could Complicate Mexico Talks July 28, 2026 | 🟡 📰 Trump's former trade chief tells farm media that Mexico — not Canada — will be the biggest test in USMCA talks, folding immigration and cartels into what is supposed to be a trade review. The formula is familiar: make security the precondition, and the tariffs never have to come off. Site blocks external readers, so no quotes — the headline does the work. Source

‍REUTERS: Kia to invest $649 million to bring electric car production to Mexico July 29, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Kia will build the EV3 in Nuevo León starting August 4 — the first fully electric vehicle made and sold in Mexico by a global brand. US majors skipped it; the wire ran on regional stations like Peoria's WMBD. Ebrard framed it as an answer to US protectionism: while Washington pushes a 50% US-content rule for North American vehicles, Mexico is pulling Korean battery and EV tech into its own market. • "A significant portion is intended for the domestic market" — Sheinbaum • US proposed that "50% of the value" of North American-built vehicles originate in the US

‍SA EXPRESS-NEWS: Mexico backs off lawsuit threat against SpaceX over Starship debris July 30, 2026 | 🟡 📰 Mexico opted for coordination over court after Starship explosions scattered debris along 200 miles of its coastline. The Express-News headline reads "backs off." What coordination already got: Profepa monitoring, Navy and aviation notification plans, and a US review of a flight path that would keep Starship over American territory instead of Mexico. • "for now, we have opted for coordination" — Sheinbaum • SpaceX insists the wreckage poses "no chemical, biological, or toxicological risks"

‍REUTERS: Mexico's economy grows at fastest pace since late 2020 in Q2 July 30, 2026 | 🟢 📰 INEGI's official print: GDP +1.3% q/q in Q2, +2.1% y/y — the fastest pace since late 2020, above analyst forecasts, lifted by services and farming. Reuters ran it straight, no editorializing. Same outlet, one week earlier: "Mexican economy falters in May as construction dips." A bad month gets the frown; a quarter that beats expectations gets a wire brief.

🇲🇽📈 <u>HIDALGO POSTS MEXICO'S STRONGEST GROWTH: +8.16% IN 12 MONTHS</u>

INEGI's state activity indicator is out: Hidalgo grew 8.16% over the last twelve months — the fastest in Mexico, nearly three points ahead of Tamaulipas (+5.33%), with Colima in third. While most states slowed at the start of 2026, Hidalgo chained ever-stronger quarters: 2.29% in Q2 2025, 3.58% by Q4. (El Economista)
